wall-following without flexing the last two joints is paid in two geometries (both measured here on synthetic states, both also paid by iter_18, so not introduced): (a) fingers straight and parallel to the cup axis with the thumb opposite: hand_curl 1.0, env_mult 1.0 (opposition does not block it, contrary to the diagnosis' hypothesis); (b) a straight k0-k1-tip chain touching at its middle on the large cups (outer radius >= 4.6 cm): lift_off 0.87-0.97 cm -> curl 1.0; the same chain touching at the tip (the operator's straight bar) 0.03. The m18 policies wrap horizontally (pad end 115-148 deg around from the palm), so (a) needs a new approach posture; watch pad-end azimuth and finger direction vs the cup axis in the m20 replay

rim / lid contact: lift_off has no side-wall weighting (the plan does not ask for one), so a digit lying on a rim or the shaker lid can read a small lift_off; env_depth already pays such links. Check the lid/rim share in the m20 replay (c1's own note)
iter_18 residual unchanged: palm contact paid inside held and hold_grip

rule: gate PASS AND plan conformance (iter_19/improvement.md: only the per-digit curl measure changes, lift_off / follow / digit_touch x follow with FOLLOW_DEAD 0.010 and FOLLOW_SCALE 0.006; inner_share, press, CURL_FULL_SHARE, CURL_FORCE_REF removed in every form; the rest identical to iter_19/compute_reward.py by AST; symmetric, no per-finger term, no absolute force or angle target, surface fields from ctx, interface unchanged, no speed/control relaxation, iter_16/18 structure and budgets kept) AND deterministic property check (tip press < curl on the diagnosis shapes; harder tip never raises the curl; digit removal never raises it; bounded; smooth near zero) AND offline replay (e1000 and m18 e800, both judged tip press, scored as not curled)
warm_start_why: best evaluated checkpoint (fixed-tol success 0.842, goal3 0.660) and the one m19 already starts from, so an iter_20 run differs from m19 by the reward only. The diagnosis gives no reason to prefer another: e1000 predates the curl factor and scores lower on the new signal (0.159 vs 0.210), e1250 regressed (0.785). At the switch e800 loses 2.8 % of its downstream income (env_mult 0.565 -> 0.549), a smaller shock than m18's iter_16 -> iter_18 critic change. A cp_l_m19 checkpoint can replace it only after a fixed-tol eval shows it beats 0.842 (m19 has the mirrored y bound); that is the main session's call
